observations.title: Sangay volcano (Ecuador)
observations.description: The Instituto Geofísico-Escuela Politécnica Nacional (IG-EPN) reported that volcanic activity at Sangay increased during 19-21 September and remained elevated, after months of low activity. An ash emission seen in satellite and webcam images rose 1.2 km above the crater rim and drifted W on 16 September. A thermal anomaly was identified in satellite images on 17 September. A sustained increase in sulfur dioxide (SO2) emissions began on 19 September; emissions peaked at around 78 and 256 tonnes per day (t/d) on 19 and 20 September, respectively. SO2 emissions rose to 1,213 t/d on 21 September, which was the highest recorded value in 2026. Both the number and amplitude of detected infrasound signals increased at 1900 on 20 September. During 19-21 September gas-and-ash plumes rose as high as 3 km above the crater rim and drifted less than 100 km mainly W and SW, though plumes drifted N and NW late on 20 September. Minor ashfall was reported in Columbe (44 km WNW), Guarguallá Chico (25 km NW), and Riobamba (51 km NW), Chimborazo province. The ejection of incandescent material onto the upper flanks was observed during dark hours. Ash plumes rose as high as 3 km above the summit and drifted NW, WSW, and SW during 22-23 September. The Secretaría de Gestión de Riesgos (SGR) maintained the Alert Level at Yellow (the second highest level on a four-color scale). Sources: Instituto Geofísico-Escuela Politécnica Nacional (IG-EPN) ,Secretaría de Gestión de Riesgos (SGR)
